query: What is the current state of the 2026 Maine Senate race between Susan Collins and Democratic candidates? Who is the Democratic nominee or frontrunner, and what do recent head-to-head polls show as of July 2026?
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings on the 2026 Maine Senate race:

**The Situation (as of July 15, 2026):** The race is in an unusual state of flux. Republican incumbent **Susan Collins** is seeking a sixth term, but there is currently **no Democratic nominee**.

**What happened:** Graham Platner won the Democratic primary June 9 (beating Gov. Janet Mills) but **withdrew July 8–10** after sexual assault accusations and other scandals. Maine Democrats must name a replacement by July 27, via a **one-day nominating convention of 601 delegates on July 25 in Bangor**.

**Frontrunner:** No official frontrunner, but **Troy Jackson** (former state Senate president) is the most-cited favorite among a field of at least 7 candidates (also Nirav Shah, Shenna Bellows, Jordan Wood, and others).

**Polling:**
- Pre-withdrawal, Platner vs. Collins was a **dead heat** (RCP average: Platner 48.2%, Collins 47.2%). The trend turned against Platner in late June, with Fox News (Jun 23–27) becoming the first major poll to show **Collins ahead (50–47)**.
- Replacement-candidate polls (Z to A Research, ~July 9) show Shah (+1), Bellows (tied), and Jackson (–1) all within a point of Collins; a Platner internal poll showed Jackson strongest at 49–44.

**Markets & ratings:** Polymarket's "Maine Senate Election Winner" now prices the **Republican (Collins) side at 65.5%**, up sharply from ~52.5% before Platner's exit. Cook rates it Toss-up; Inside Elections says Tilt Republican.

All findings, sources, and quantitative data points have been recorded via the structured output tool.

key_facts: Republican incumbent Susan Collins is seeking a sixth term; she was the only Republican to qualify for the primary ballot.
Graham Platner won the Democratic primary June 9, 2026 (beating Gov. Janet Mills) but withdrew July 8-10, 2026 amid sexual assault accusations and other controversies.
As of July 15, 2026 there is NO Democratic nominee; the Maine Democratic Party must name a replacement by July 27 via a one-day nominating convention of 601 delegates on July 25, 2026 in Bangor.
At least 7 Democrats are competing to replace Platner: Troy Jackson, Jordan Wood, Nirav Shah, Shenna Bellows, Dan Kleban, David Costello, and Paige Loud.
Troy Jackson (former state Senate president) is the most frequently cited convention favorite/frontrunner, though there is no official frontrunner.
Pre-withdrawal RealClearPolling/270toWin average had Platner 48.2% vs Collins 47.2% (Platner +1), effectively a dead heat.
NYT/Portland Press Herald/Siena poll (Jun 19-26, 608 LV) showed Platner +2 (49-47), within margin of error.
Fox News poll (Jun 23-27, 1,003 RV) showed Collins +3 (50-47) - the first major poll with Collins ahead.
A Z to A Research poll (~July 9, 988 LV) of replacements: Shah 47-46 over Collins, Bellows tied 47-47, Jackson trailed 47-48.
A Platner internal flash poll (via Politico) showed Jackson strongest, leading Collins 49-44.
Race ratings: Cook Political Report Toss-up; Inside Elections Tilt Republican.
Maine uses ranked-choice voting; Democrats have not won a Maine Senate race since 1988; Maine is the only GOP Senate seat in a state Trump never won.
Polymarket 'Maine Senate Election Winner' priced the Republican (Collins) side at 65.5% on July 15, up from ~52.5% on July 4, reflecting Platner's withdrawal.
Polymarket: Democrats 45.5% to win Senate control 2026; Democrats 83.5% to win the House 2026 (as of July 15, 2026).
